task: F33 template factory showroom compiler provenance and route catalog evidence projection, preserving true owner approval

assuranceCeiling.rationale: Candidate route provenance and showroom evidence are existing compiler outputs. Passing them to the browser gate is required but not sufficient for separate Preview owner-login proof and Product Owner approval; this unit must not invent rows or weaken acceptance criteria.

acceptanceCriteria: QA catalog candidate provenance is exactly the canonical Factory compiler's own report object.
QA catalog showroom evidence is nonempty and exactly matches existing report rows for the same template key/version.
Production and legacy non-Factory template entries do not acquire misleading candidate provenance.
Browser acceptance and Product Owner login proof remain separate external requirements, never auto-passed by compiler metadata.
invariants: Factory catalog may only copy, not invent or reinterpret, compiler provenance and showroom evidence.
Every showroom row is tied to the genuine canonical package Page Schema and route.
The catalog remains gated behind VISUAL_FIDELITY_QA and its 404 behavior is retained.
No hidden auto-accept flag, runtime renderer change or production activation.
forbiddenStates: Synthetic showroom rows or fixed strings masquerade as compiler-generated proof.
Missing/failing showroom validation is accepted as pass.
A Factory candidate is released solely because its catalog has two metadata fields.
Unapproved production-facing template activation is introduced.

failureModes: The response serializer drops metadata fields despite the compiler's completed report.
Incorrect candidate identity maps metadata from a different template version.
Product Owner handoff is permitted from a fake metadata object without journey proof.
QA flag is disabled, but the route becomes public.
Extra or incomplete showroom rows obscure missing shopper routes.
edgeCases: Loot Vault v2 candidate exact report and 20 showroom surfaces.
Noncandidate Playroom and quality candidate catalog entries.
A compiled Factory candidate fails productOwnerReady and should be excluded.
Showroom row lacks pageKey, presentationAuthority or entrypoint and must stay blocked.

alternatives.summary: Project compiled report provenance and showroom rows in the existing catalog response, with exact-copy tests.
alternatives.reason: Repairs the observable missing fields at the consumer boundary without changing source-of-truth or acceptance.

alternatives.summary: Add default catalog provenance and synthetic showroom rows for missing data.
alternatives.reason: Would produce counterfeit proof even when the compiled canonical package is incomplete.

alternatives.summary: Mark candidates factory-identity-pinned or showroom-passed when browser cases pass.
alternatives.reason: Lowers the Product Owner gate and loses the independent source/route provenance contract.

specialistReviews.finding: The Factory compile report is already canonical metadata authority, while the QA route drops its provenance and showroom rows.
specialistReviews.resolution: Project the original report properties unchanged, avoiding a parallel contract.

specialistReviews.finding: Adding metadata might be wrongly interpreted as production readiness or Product Owner approval.
specialistReviews.resolution: Retain the QA feature gate, source-only projection, external buyer journey and PO independent approval requirements.

specialistReviews.finding: The browser quality runner consumes catalog data and refuses Factory targets missing exact provenance and showroom fields.
specialistReviews.resolution: Assert exact serializer output against compiled reports, then let full browser/E13 runtime proof independently validate.

challenge.scenario: Factory compiler has correct provenance but catalog omits it.
challenge.resolution: Expose report.provenance unchanged on Factory entries only.

challenge.scenario: A generated showroom has 20 valid surface rows, none sent downstream.
challenge.resolution: Pass through report.showroomEvidence as a copied array of original rows.

challenge.scenario: Another template version has different source metadata.
challenge.finding: A hand-authored key or default could certify the wrong candidate.
challenge.resolution: Bind metadata to the same build result and verify key/version through test.

challenge.scenario: QA endpoint is disabled outside gated environment.
challenge.finding: Accidental exposure reveals internal candidate report.
challenge.resolution: Preserve the existing VISUAL_FIDELITY_QA flag and assert 404 disabled.

challenge.scenario: Compiler identifies a structurally invalid candidate.
challenge.finding: Adding transport must not override productOwnerReady filtering.
challenge.resolution: Do not change compiler readiness or catalog exclusion guards.

challenge.scenario: Candidate is catalog-pinned but Product Owner login journey has not run.
challenge.finding: Gate may be misread as final acceptance.
challenge.resolution: Retain separate owner Preview gate and honest PARTIALLY_VERIFIED until proof.

proofPlan: Test the actual QA GET route response under QA flag against immutable Factory compiler report provenance and showroom evidence.
Verify non-Factory entries unchanged and QA disabled returns 404, preserving fail-closed behavior.
Run Plan Before Code with full known-failure replay, Source tests, TypeScript, build, Factory Browser 14x3 and E13 proof where required.
Require independently verified Product Owner login and exact-head Preview before any end-to-end Factory closure; do not invent credentials.
Keep F31 and F32 draft, no merge to main, no production or Supabase mutations.

semanticExecutionRoute.request: F33 compiler report metadata catalog projection

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: The canonical Factory candidate compiler returns accurate provenance and showroom evidence, but its quality-catalog API omits both, causing source-bound browser acceptance to reject the candidate as not pinned without running a Product Owner journey.
observableOutcomes: Factory catalog exposes the exact compiler provenance for gaming.loot-vault@2 with no inferred values.
Factory catalog exposes the complete exact compiler showroom rows and rejects placeholder or missing authority.
The Quality Gate still determines candidate identity and showroom validity from those rows; owner login and browser proofs remain independently required.
unresolvedRisks: A corrected QA catalog does not prove authenticated Vercel Product Owner preview without separately executed journey.
Changes to the catalog runtime can require exact-head Vercel Preview and fresh 14x3 browser evidence; no stale source is sufficient.
The existing Loot Vault visual fidelity and Product Owner sign-off are distinct from this transport repair.

in: exact generated provenance and showroom rows

requirements.requirement: The QA candidate manifest must receive exact genuine compiler provenance and showroom route evidence without claiming separate Product Owner approval.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Synthetic identity/showroom metadata or bypass of login and external Factory gates must never yield Product Owner approval.

notes: F33 scoped supplier-to-consumer Factory proof handoff, stacked on F32 PR #1238 (and F31 #1236). An existing compiler creates provenance and showroom evidence but the QA catalog omits both. Transport only genuine report fields, never self-certify Product Owner journey or promote a template. No main/production/Supabase/Vercel changes. Full known-failure replay is mandatory because of architecture note.
